title: Guarding withBase and withoutBase against false prefix matches
premise: `withBase` and `withoutBase` decided a path "has" the base purely with `input.startsWith(_base)`. That matches too much: a path like `/admin-dashboard` starts with the string `/admin`, so the base was treated as already present. `withBase` then returned the input untouched (base silently dropped), and `withoutBase` sliced off the first 6 characters and re-prepended a slash, turning `/admin-dashboard` into the nonsense `/-dashboard`. The change adds a one-character lookahead: the character right after the base must be nothing, `/`, or `?` for the prefix to count as a real base boundary.
verdict: The change makes one claim true: a base only counts as a prefix of a path when it ends on a segment boundary (end of string, `/`, or `?`). Where it doesn't, `withBase` now prepends the base (`/admin-dashboard` + base `/admin/` → `/admin/admin-dashboard`) and `withoutBase` now leaves the path alone (`/admin-dashboard` minus base `/admin/` stays `/admin-dashboard`) instead of producing `/-dashboard`. Four new tests are direct fail→pass evidence (two per function), and the twenty-eight pre-existing pass→pass tests show genuine prefixes (`/admin/dashboard`, `/api?test`), non-matches, protocol URLs, and empty bases are all untouched because their lookahead char is `/`, `?`, or absent. The run reaches both changed functions on both sides, so no code is unexercised. Risk is low and local: the only behavioural shift is for callers who previously relied on the buggy "starts-with-string" matching — any such caller now gets the corrected, boundary-aware result, which is the intended fix. Worth approving; the only thing to confirm by eye is that `#` fragments (which neither test exercises) are an acceptable non-boundary char, i.e. `/admin#x` is intentionally treated as not having base `/admin`.

repo.title: fix(withBase, withoutBase): prevent false prefix matches

chapters.title: withBase, where nothing should change
chapters.before: The first ten cases flow through `withBase` untouched: base `/` or `""` returns the input via `isEmptyURL`; `https://test.com` returns early via `hasProtocol`; a real prefix like input `/base` against base `/base/` has `input.startsWith('/base')` true and returns `/base`; a non-match like `/bar` with base `/foo` falls to `joinURL` → `/foo/bar`.
chapters.after: Identical results. In every one of these cases the character after the base is either absent or `/`, so even though the new `nextChar` lookahead now runs on the `startsWith` branch, it still permits the early return. Outputs match the base run exactly.
facts: withBase returns input unchanged when isEmptyURL(base) or hasProtocol(input) is true, before and after.
For a genuine prefix the early return still fires because nextChar is undefined or '/'.
For a non-prefix the code falls to joinURL(_base, input) on both sides.

chapters.title: withBase stops dropping the base on a false prefix
chapters.before: Input `/admin-dashboard` with base `/admin/` (and again with base `/admin`): `_base` = `/admin`, and `input.startsWith('/admin')` is true, so the function returned the input unchanged — `/admin-dashboard` — silently dropping the base. The test expected `/admin/admin-dashboard`, so it raised AssertionError.
chapters.after: `nextChar = input[6]` is `-`, which is not undefined, `/`, or `?`, so the early return is skipped. Control falls to `joinURL('/admin', ['/admin-dashboard'])`, which runs `isNonEmptyURL` then `withTrailingSlash('/admin')` → `/admin/` and yields `/admin/admin-dashboard`. The two broken tests now pass. The genuine cases alongside them — `/admin/admin-dashboard` and `/admin/dashboard` (nextChar `/`) — still short-circuit and return the input unchanged on both sides.
facts: withoutTrailingSlash turns both base `/admin/` and `/admin` into `_base` = `/admin`.
The guard `!nextChar || nextChar === '/' || nextChar === '?'` decides whether the prefix is a real boundary.
When the guard fails, joinURL re-adds the base, producing `/admin/admin-dashboard`.
A trailing-boundary prefix (`/admin/dashboard`, nextChar '/') is unaffected and still returns input.

open_questions.question: Does the inverse operation, withoutBase, get the same boundary guard, and what did its false-prefix bug produce before?

chapters.title: withoutBase, where nothing should change
chapters.before: Thirteen cases trim or pass through as before: genuine prefixes slice correctly (`/base/a` minus `/base` → `/a`), a query boundary is respected (`/api?test` minus `/api` → `/?test`, nextChar `?`), non-matches are returned (`/bar` minus `/foo` → `/bar`), and empty-base / protocol inputs pass straight through.
chapters.after: Identical. In each case the character after `_base` is `/`, `?`, undefined, or the input never matches the base at all, so the new `nextChar` guard never changes the outcome. Outputs match the base run.
facts: withoutBase returns input unchanged when isEmptyURL(base) or when input does not start with _base.
The `?` query boundary is an accepted boundary char, so `/api?test` minus `/api` still becomes `/?test`.
Genuine prefixes still slice off `_base` and normalise the leading slash.

chapters.title: withoutBase stops mangling a false prefix
chapters.before: Input `/admin-dashboard` with base `/admin/` (and with base `/admin`): `_base` = `/admin`, `input.startsWith('/admin')` is true, so it sliced the first 6 chars to `-dashboard` and, since that doesn't start with `/`, prepended one → `/-dashboard`. The expected `/admin-dashboard` never came; the test raised AssertionError.
chapters.after: The new lookahead runs before the slice: `nextChar = input[6]` is `-`, and `nextChar && nextChar !== '/' && nextChar !== '?'` is true, so the function returns the input unchanged — `/admin-dashboard`. Both broken tests pass. The genuine neighbours still trim: `/admin/admin-dashboard` minus `/admin/` → `/admin-dashboard`, and `/admin/dashboard` → `/dashboard` (nextChar `/`).
facts: The guard sits after the startsWith check and before the slice, so a false prefix now returns input instead of `/-dashboard`.
This mirrors the withBase guard from chapter 2 with inverted logic: there it blocks an early return, here it adds one.
Genuine prefixes with nextChar '/' are still sliced and re-slashed as before.

answers.answer: Yes: withoutBase gets the same boundary check with inverted logic. Before the fix its false-prefix bug produced `/-dashboard` from `/admin-dashboard`; after, the guard returns the input unchanged.
